titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§105–108: The Muster Against the Merkid
about: Four sections, one campaign taking shape. In §105 Temüjin sends Qasar and Belgütei to Jamuqa; To'oril's word follows, and Jamuqa answers with his grief for Börte and a plan against the three Merkid chiefs, naming where each lies. In §106 Jamuqa sends his own answer, a list of the gear he has readied and a place to meet. §107 has the armies set out, and §108 brings them to Botoqan-Boqorji, where Jamuqa, three days early, reproaches them for being late.

sentences.t: Temüžin, Qasar, Belgütei γurban Toγ̇oril Qān-(n)ača qarižu ger-tür(i)-jen kürčü
sentences.l: Temüžin, Qasar, Belgütei, the three, from Toγ̇oril Qān returning, to-their-own-tent arriving,
sentences.i: Temüjin, Qasar and Belgütei, the three of them, came back from Qan To'oril and reached their own tent.
sentences.n: A plain converb chain: qarižu 'turning back' and kürčü 'arriving' hang on what follows. Ming 囘著 and 到着 mark them with 着, its sign for the converb. Qān-(n)ača is the ablative -(n)ača, 'from', glossed 自; the title qān stands after the name, Toγ̇oril Qān. In ger-tür(i)-jen the dative-locative -tür(i) (Ming 行) is followed by the reflexive-possessive -jen, 'to their own tent'; the (i) is Shiratori's. The unit stops here because the clause is not finished: the main verb is ilerün in the next one.

sentences.t: Temüžin Žamuqa-dur Qasar, Belgütei qojar-i ilerün, Žamuqa anda-da ügüle keġen ügüležü ilerün,
sentences.l: Temüžin, to Jamuqa, Qasar, Belgütei, the two (acc.), sending: "Jamuqa, to the sworn-brother say" saying, speaking, sending,
sentences.i: Temüjin sent Qasar and Belgütei, the two, to Jamuqa, telling them to say to his sworn brother Jamuqa:
sentences.n: Temüžin is the subject; qojar-i (Ming 兩箇 行) is the pair Qasar and Belgütei as object, and Žamuqa-dur (行) is the place they are sent to. ilerün is ile- 'send' with the converb of time -rün (Ming 使去 'send'); the second ilerün is glossed only 去 'go', so 'going' is possible there. ügüle is the bare stem used as an imperative, 'say!', and keġen closes the quotation. anda is the 'sworn brother', the pledged friend of the chronicle, here Jamuqa. The message follows in the next units.

sentences.t: γurban Merkid-te irežü oro-ban hoγtorγu bolγaγdaγ̇a bi.
sentences.l: Three, by-the-Merkid, having-come, own-place empty was-made, I.
sentences.i: "The three Merkid came, and my own place was left empty.
sentences.n: The Ming marks Merkid-te with 行, the dative-locative marker, and the verb is a passive, so I read the dative as the agent, 'by the Merkid'; that is a reading, not a certainty. oro-ban (Ming 位, 'position') is the place one holds; it is the same spelling as oro 'hollow of the chest' used in a later unit. The message begins here; its closing quotation mark stands on bida in word 45. bolγaγdaγ̇a is bol- 'become' with a causative -γa- and a passive -γda-, 'was made'; the last ending is uncertain.

sentences.t: Onor nigenten busutu bida ösül(i)-jen ker ösekün
sentences.l: Nock one-ers, not-so are we? Own-feud how to-avenge?
sentences.i: Are we not of one nock? How shall we avenge our feud?
sentences.n: Hard to read; I give it as two questions. Onor is the arrow-nock (the Ming 扣子 means a button or fastening; I take it as the notch, from onolaba 'to nock' later in the text), and nigenten is nigen 'one' with the collective -ten, 'the ones of one nock', that is, men of one stock. busutu (Ming 不是有的麽, 'is it not so?') is the form of a rhetorical question; I cannot analyse it with confidence. ösül(i)-jen is 'one's own feud' (Ming 讐 自的); ösekün is a form of ösü- 'repay, avenge' in an ending I do not know, compare hačilaqun in a later unit.

sentences.t: Erte üdür Jesügei Qān ečige-de min-u tusa said kigdegsen-i sedkižü nököčesü bi.
sentences.l: Formerly, day: Jesügei Qān to-father, my help good done (acc.), thinking, companion-let-me-be, I.
sentences.i: In the old days I did my father Yesügei Qan good service. Remembering it, I will be your companion.
sentences.n: To'oril's words, sent to Jamuqa by way of Temüjin's messengers. ečige-de is 'father' in the dative (Ming 父 行), so the old Qan is called 'father' (as the elder sworn friend, I take it); min-u is 'my' placed after its noun; tusa said is 'help, good'; kigdegsen-i is ki- 'do' with a passive and the past participle plus the accusative, 'what was done' (Ming 被做了的 行). I read the passive as the service done by the speaker, but the grammar leaves the doer open. nököčesü is nököče- 'be a companion' with the optative -sü, 'let me be a companion'. There is no opening quotation mark in the print; the closing one stands at the end of word 95.

sentences.t: Qojar tümed bolžu baraγ̇un γar bolun morilasu.
sentences.l: Two tümens making, right hand being, let me mount.
sentences.i: I will mount with two tümens, and be your right hand.
sentences.n: Two tümens are two units of ten thousand men (tümed is tümen with the plural -d, Ming 萬每). bolun is bol- 'become' with the converb -un, 'being'; with γar 'hand' and baraγ̇un 'right' it is 'being the right hand'. morilasu is mori 'horse' made a verb with -la- and given the optative -su, 'let me mount'.

sentences.i: Send word to my younger brother Jamuqa.
sentences.n: deġü-de is deġü 'younger brother' in the dative (Ming 弟 行), the title the older man gives Jamuqa. keleležü is kele- 'speak' with -le- and the converb -žü. ile is the bare stem of ile- 'send' used as an imperative; Ming 去.

sentences.i: Let my younger brother Jamuqa mount with two tümens.
sentences.n: morilatuγai is the same verb as morilasu, now with the third-person optative -tuγai (Ming 敎 上馬, 'cause to mount'), so 'let him mount'. qojar tümed (Ming 二 萬每) is 'two tümens'. The speech is To'oril's, still addressed to the messengers.

sentences.t: Qamtudqu bolžaγ̇an Žamuqa deġü-dēče boltuγai" keġebe.
sentences.l: The joint appointment, Jamuqa younger-brother-from, let it be" said.
sentences.i: Let him fix the joint meeting," he said.
sentences.n: Qamtudqu is a participle of a verb I give as qamtud- 'be together' (Ming 相合的); bolžaγ̇an is 'appointment, meeting' (Ming 約會), and I do not know the exact ending. deġü-dēče has the ablative -dēče, 'from', so the arrangement of the meeting is to come 'from' Jamuqa. boltuγai is bol- with the optative, 'let it be'. The closing quotation mark stands on boltuγai in the print.

sentences.t: Ösül(i)-jen ösen Uduid, Uwas Merkid-i ülüdkežü Üžin-Börte-jen aburaja
sentences.l: Own-feud avenging, Uduid, Uwas Merkid (acc.) destroying, Üjin-Börte own rescue-let-us.
sentences.i: Let us avenge our feud, destroy the Uduid and Uwas Merkid, and rescue Üjin Börte.
sentences.n: ösen has the Ming gloss 報 'repay'; I give it ösü- with an ending -n, the stem being uncertain. Uduid and Uwas are clan names (Ming 姓氏) of the Merkid; Merkid-i takes the accusative. ülüdkežü is a converb 'destroying' (Ming 殘滅着). aburaja is abura- with the hortative -ja, 'let us ...'; the Ming 救 says 'rescue, save'. Üžin-Börte-jen has the reflexive-possessive, so 'our own Börte'.

sentences.l: Own-feud avenging, all the Qa'at Merkid (acc.) smashing, lady Börte own, bringing back, rescue-let-us.
sentences.i: Let us avenge our feud, break all the Qa'at Merkid, bring the lady Börte back and rescue her.
sentences.n: aburan has the Ming gloss 報 'repay', and aburaja 救 'rescue'; they look like one stem, abura-, and I cannot say how the two senses join (perhaps 'set right'). qaltačižu (Ming 破着) is 'smashing'. qariγ̇ulun is qari- 'turn back' with the causative -γ̇ul- and the converb -un, 'making her return'; the Ming gloss is only 囘着. Börte-jüġen is the reflexive-possessive in its longer form, 'her own'. aburaja appears twice with the Ming gloss 救咱.

sentences.t: Edöġe tere gölme dabšiqui-dur köġürge-jin daγ̇u bolγažu kökideg Toγtoγ̇a Nuγ̇ura keġer-e bi že.
sentences.l: Now, that saddle-cloth when-slapping, drum's sound making, easily-startled Toqto'a, Nu'ura steppe-on, is, so.
sentences.i: Now Toqto'a, who is so easily startled that the slap of a saddle-cloth sounds to him like a drum, is out on the steppe of Nu'ura.
sentences.n: The Ming reads tere gölme dabšiqui-dur köġürge-jin daγ̇u bolγažu as 'when that saddle-cloth is slapped, making a drum's sound', and kökideg as 轻驚動的 'easily startled'; so the epithet. I put the figure in i as the English needs it. keġer-e is keġer 'open ground' with the dative-locative (Ming 野甸行). bi is 'is' here (Ming 有), not 'I', and že is a particle of assent, 'so'. Nuγ̇ura is a place name, 地名.

sentences.t: Dabčitu qor darbalžaqui-dur daižiγči Dair-Usun edöġe Orqon, Seleṅge qojar-un žaγ̇ura Talγun Aral-a bi že.
sentences.l: Lidded quiver when-shaken, rebelling Dair-Usun, now Orqon, Selenge of-the-two between Talqun islet-on is, so.
sentences.i: Dair-Usun, who rebels at the rattle of a lidded quiver, is now on the island of Talqun, between the Orqon and the Selenge.

Aral-a is 'island, islet' (Ming (洲)) with the dative-locative. Talγun is a place name.

sentences.t: Qamqa ulsun keisküi-dür qara hoi temečegči Qaγ̇atai-Darmala edöġe Qaraži keġer-e bi že;
sentences.l: Qamqa, ulsun when-the-wind-blows, black wood contender, Qa'atai-Darmala, now Qaraji steppe-on is, so;
sentences.i: Qa'atai-Darmala, who contends with the black wood when the wind blows on the qamqa and ulsun, is now on the steppe of Qaraji;
sentences.n: Qamqa (Ming 蓬 'fleabane, tumbleweed') and ulsun (蒿 'wormwood') are two dry steppe plants; keisküi-dür (風刮 時) is 'at the blowing of the wind'. temečegči (Ming 爭的) is 'one who strives, contends'. The line is the figure of a man who starts at a rustle, like Toqto'a and Dair-Usun, but how 'qara hoi temečegči' belongs to the plants I am not sure: the Ming gives no joint. Qaraži is a place name, 地名.

sentences.t: edöġe bida dötelen Kilqo müren-(n)i kiṅgüs Saqal-Bajan esen atuγai.
sentences.l: Now we, straight across, the Kilqo river (acc.) cutting-across, Saqal-Bajan safe let-be.
sentences.i: Now let us go straight across the Kilqo river, and let Saqal-Bajan stay safe.

Saqal-Bajan is glossed 猪鬃草 'boar-bristle grass'; saqal is 'beard', bajan 'rich'; it may be a name of a place or a person, or just the plant. esen is 'safe, whole' and atuγai is a- 'be' with the optative -tuγai, 'let it stay'.

sentences.t: Sal hujažu oroja.
sentences.l: Raft tying, let-us-enter.
sentences.i: Let us tie rafts and board them.
sentences.n: sal is a raft (Ming 筏子), hujažu is huja- 'tie, knot' with the converb -žu, and oroja is oro- 'enter' with the hortative -ja. The Ming for oroja is 入咱 'let us enter'; the English 'board' is my reading of a raft.

sentences.t: Tere kökideg Toγtoγ̇a-jin erüge deġere in-ü orožu erkin eġede in-ü embürü daγ̇arižu
sentences.l: That easily-startled Toqto'a's smoke-hole above, his, entering, the essential door-frame his collapsing, colliding,
sentences.i: Let us come in at the top of the smoke-hole of that startled Toqto'a, and strike so that the frame of his tent falls in,
sentences.n: erüge is the roof-window or smoke-hole of a tent (Ming 天窗 'skylight'), and deġere is 'on top, above'; in-ü is 'his' set after its noun. eġede is 'door, door-frame'; here the Ming says 帳房骨子 'tent frame'. embürü and daγ̇arižu are converbs (Ming 塌了 'fallen in', 撞着 'colliding'); the stems embür- and quγ̇ur- are inferred from the Ming. The subject is 'we' from the hortatives that surround the clause.

sentences.t: eme köġün in-ü ečültele qaγ̇uluja;
sentences.l: Wife, son, his, until-ended, let-us-ruin;
sentences.i: until his wives and sons are finished, and let us ruin him;
sentences.n: ečültele is ečül- 'be finished' (stem inferred, Ming 盡絕了) with the converb -tele, 'until'. qaγ̇uluja is qaγ̇ul- 'plunder, ruin' with the hortative -ja; the Ming gives 毀了咱 here and 毀滅咱 at the end of the section.

sentences.l: Fortune door-frame his breaking, colliding,
sentences.i: let us strike so that the door-post of his good fortune breaks,
sentences.n: qutuγ is 'blessing, fortune' (Ming 福神的, 'of the fortune-spirit'), so eġede is the door-frame where the fortune-spirit lives; here the Ming has 門框. quγ̇uru (Ming 折了) is quγ̇ur- 'to break' with the converb -u; the stem is inferred.

sentences.t: qotola ulus-i in-ü qoγ̇osun boltala qaγ̇uluja.
sentences.l: All, people (acc.) his, until-empty-becoming, let-us-ruin.
sentences.i: and let us ruin all his people until nothing is left of them."
sentences.n: qotola (Ming 都行) is 'all, altogether'. boltala is bol- with the converb -tala, 'until it becomes', Ming 到了; qoγ̇osun is 'empty'. The section ends here; Jamuqa speaks again at the head of §106 (basa, 'again').

sentences.t: Žamuqa basa ügülerün: "Temüžin anda, Toγ̇oril Qān aqa qojar-a ügüle" keġen ügülerün:
sentences.l: Jamuqa again speaking: "Temüžin sworn-brother, Toγ̇oril Qān elder-brother, to-the-two say" saying, speaking:
sentences.i: Jamuqa spoke again: "Say to the two of them, to my sworn brother Temüjin and to my elder brother Qan To'oril," and he continued:
sentences.n: The speaker is Jamuqa, talking to the messengers, who are to carry his answer; qojar-a (Ming 兩箇行) is 'to the two'. ügüle is again the bare stem as an imperative, 'say!'. aqa is 'elder brother', the title Jamuqa gives To'oril. The speech after this is a message to be delivered, so the Mongol speaks in the first person while the carriers recite it.

sentences.t: "Bi bürün qaraγ̇atu tuk(i)-jan sačuba bi.
sentences.l: I, as-for, far-seeing banner my-own sprinkled, I.
sentences.i: "As for me, I have made offering to my far-seeing banner.
sentences.n: Bi bürün, 'I being' (Ming 我 呵, 'as for me'), is a topic phrase. qaraγ̇atu is a stem I infer from qara- 'look', meaning 'seen from far', with -tu 'having'; the Ming 遠看見的 is 'seen from far'. tuk(i)-jan has the Ming 英頭, 'hero-head', and I take the word as the standard or banner; the stem is uncertain. sačuba is saču- 'sprinkle' in the past; the Ming 祭 shows an offering was made to it, presumably a libation.

morph.gloss: converb of time: being; after bi, 'as for me' (Ming 呵)
a far view (stem inferred from qara- 'to look'; Ming 遠看見的 'seen from afar') [遠看(見)的]
standard, banner (so read; the Ming 英頭 is 'hero-head' and the stem is uncertain) [英頭 自的行]
to sprinkle a libation, to sacrifice (stem inferred; Ming 祭了也) [祭了也]

sentences.t: Qara buγa-jin arasun(i)-jar bürigsen bürkiren büküi daγ̇utu köġürge-ban deledbe bi.
sentences.l: Black bull's hide-with covered, booming being, voiced drum my-own beaten, I.
sentences.i: I have beaten my drum, covered in black bull's hide, with its booming voice.
sentences.n: Qara buγa-jin is 'of the black bull' (Ming 强牛 的), arasun(i)-jar the instrumental of 'hide' (Ming 皮子 敎, where 敎 marks 'with'). bürigsen (幔了的) is 'covered'; bürkiren (鼕鼕) is a sound word, 'boom-boom'; büküi is 'being'. daγ̇utu is daγ̇u 'voice' with -tu, 'voice-having', that is, sounding. köġürge-ban is the drum with the reflexive-possessive -ban; deledbe is deled- 'beat' in the past (stem inferred).

morph.gloss: bull (Ming 强牛 'strong ox') [强牛 的]
skin, hide (noun; Ming 皮子) [皮子敎]
instrumental: with, by means of (back-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's)
to cover, to stretch over (stem inferred; Ming 幔了的) [幔了的]
booming, drumming (sound word; Ming 鼕鼕 'boom-boom'; perhaps bürkire- + -n) [鼕鼕]
to beat, to strike (stem inferred; Ming 打了也) [打了也]

sentences.t: Qara qurdun(i)-jan unuba bi.
sentences.l: Black own-fast-horse rode, I.
sentences.i: I have mounted my black fast horse.
sentences.n: qurdun means 'fast' and also 'a fast horse' (Ming 快馬). The reflexive -(i)jan (自的行) again: 'my own'. unuba is unu- 'ride' in the past. A run of short parallel lines follows: each names a piece of gear and a verb of readiness.

morph.gloss: fast; a fast horse (Ming 快馬) [快馬 自的行]

sentences.t: Qataṅγu deġel(i)-jen emüsbe bi.
sentences.l: Steel-hard own-coat put-on, I.
sentences.i: I have put on my steel-hard coat.
sentences.n: qataṅγu is the Ming 鋼硬 'steel-hard'; qatan in the next unit is 鋼 'steel'. deġel is a long robe or coat; I take armour from 'steel-hard' and the setting, since the Ming says only 衣裳 'clothes'. emüsbe is emüs- 'put on, wear' in the past.

morph.gloss: steel-hard, hardened (adjective; Ming 鋼硬 'hard as steel') [鋼硬]
to put on, to wear [穿了也]

sentences.t: Qatan žida-ban bariba bi.
sentences.l: Steel own-spear taken, I.
sentences.i: I have taken up my steel spear.
sentences.n: žida-ban is žida 'spear' with the reflexive-possessive -ban; bariba is bari- 'take hold of' in the past (Ming 拿了也).

morph.gloss: to take hold of, to grasp [拿了也]

sentences.t: Qadqurasutu sumun(i)-jan onolaba bi.
sentences.l: Qadqurasu-having own-arrow nocked, I.
sentences.i: I have set my arrow to the string.
sentences.n: qadqurasutu has the Ming gloss 有挑皮的, which I cannot resolve; it is probably a kind of arrow-head, but I only guess that from the context. onolaba is onola- 'put on the nock' from onor 'nock', Ming 扣了也. qadqurasutu is left untranslated in i.

morph.gloss: (stem unclear; Ming 有挑皮的 'having a lifted skin'; some kind of arrow-head, uncertain) [有挑皮的]
to nock, to fit to the string (from onor 'nock'; Ming 扣了) [扣了也]

sentences.t: Qaγ̇ad- Merkid-tür qadquldun morilaja, böġed keġen ügüle.
sentences.l: Qa'at-Merkid-against fighting, let-us-mount, then saying, say!
sentences.i: Let us ride and fight the Qa'at Merkid. Say so.
sentences.n: Qaγ̇ad- ends in a hyphen in the print because the word is broken at the line; it carries on into Merkid-tür (Ming 種名 行, 'against the Merkid'). qadquldun is qadqul- 'fight' with an ending I do not know. morilaja is mori 'horse' made a verb with -la- and the hortative -ja, 'let us mount'. böġed keġen is 'then, saying'; ügüle is the imperative 'say!', which closes the message Jamuqa is giving his carriers. A second round of the same lines follows, now against the Uduid.

morph.gloss: the Qa'at, a Merkid clan (Ming 姓氏 'clan name'; the hyphen carries over to the next word) [姓氏]
the Merkid, a people [(種名) 行]

sentences.n: oroγ (Ming 黑脊 'black-spined') is a horse colour. The word qurdun is cut across two printed tokens, qur- and dun(i)-jan; the Ming glosses them as 快馬 and 自的行, so I give the second token its own entry as the second half and the reflexive.

sentences.n: hüdesütü has the Ming 皮穿來的 'threaded with hide'; hüdesü is my guess at the stem, 'thong, stitching' and -tü is 'having'. qujag(i)-jan is armour (Ming 甲) with the reflexive-possessive. emüsbe as above.

to put on, to wear [穿了也]

sentences.t: Oṅgitu üldü-beġen bariba bi.

sentences.i: I have taken up my hilted sabre.

to take hold of, to grasp [拿了也]

sentences.l: Nock-having own-arrow nocked, I.
sentences.i: I have fitted my notched arrow to the string.
sentences.n: onortu is onor 'nock' with -tu 'having' (Ming 扣子 有的); onolaba is the verb from it. The same shape as qadqurasutu above.

sentences.t: Uduid-Merkid-tür üküldüje böġed keġen ügüle.

sentences.i: Let us ride and fight the Uduid Merkid to the death. Say so.
sentences.n: üküldüje has the Ming 捨死厮殺咱 'staking death, fight'; I give it ükül 'death' with a verb ending -dü- (reciprocal, uncertain) and the hortative -je. uduid-merkid-tür is the name of the clan with the people name and the dative-locative.

sentences.t: Toγ̇oril Qān aqa morilarun Burqan-Qaldun-u ebür(i)-jer Temüžin anda-ji daγ̇ariγ̇ad irežü Onan müren-(n)ü teriġün-e Botoqan-Boγ̇orži-da bolžalduja
sentences.l: Toγ̇oril Qān elder-brother when-mounting, Burqan-Qaldun's front-along, Temüžin sworn-brother (acc.) passing-by, coming, Onan river's head-at, Botoqan-Boγ̇orži-at, let-us-fix-a-meeting,
sentences.i: When Qan To'oril, my elder brother, mounts, let him come along the front of Burqan Qaldun, pass by my sworn brother Temüjin, and let us fix a meeting at Botoqan-Boqorji, at the head of the Onan river,
sentences.n: ebür(i)-jer: ebür is 'front' (also 'bosom'), here the south, near face of the mountain, and -jer is an ending with the shape of the instrumental that the Ming (前行) renders 'along'. daγ̇ariγ̇ad (Ming 經過) is 'having passed'. anda-ji is the accusative of anda, so Temüjin is the one passed. bolžalduja is bolžal 'appointment' made a verb, with the hortative -ja (Ming 約會咱). Botoqan-Boγ̇orži is the name of the place (地名).

morph.gloss: To'oril, a man's name (personal name) [(人)名]
ruler, khan (title, set after the name) [皇帝]

sentences.t: endēče morilarun Onan müren öġede anda-jin ulus ende bi.
sentences.l: From-here when-mounting, Onan river up, the sworn-brother's people here are.
sentences.i: When I mount from here and go up the Onan, my sworn brother's people are here.
sentences.n: endēče is ene 'this' in the ablative with a long vowel, 'from here', Ming 自這裏. öġede (逆着) is 'upstream, up'. anda-jin ulus is 'sworn-brother's people'. bi is 'is, are' (Ming 有), not 'I'.

morph.gloss: this; here the locative stem end- [自這裏]
the Onan, the river of Chinggis's homeland (Ming 河名) [河名]
sworn brother, pledged friend [契合 的]
is, are (verb, short form; Ming 有) [有]

sentences.t: Anda-jin ulus-ača nigen tümen, bi endēče nigen tümen qojar tümen bolžu
sentences.l: Sworn-brother's people-from one tümen, I from-here one tümen, two tümens making,
sentences.i: From my sworn brother's people, one tümen, and from here, one tümen of my own: making two tümens,
sentences.n: ulus-ača is the ablative (Ming 百姓 裏), tümen 'ten thousand' as a body of men. bi endēče nigen tümen is 'I, from here, one tümen'. The sentence goes on in the next unit with the verbs.

morph.gloss: sworn brother, pledged friend [契合 的]
this; here the locative stem end- [這裏 自]

sentences.t: Onan müren öġede odču Botoqan-Boγ̇orži-da bolžal γažar-a neiledüje keġen ügüležü ilebe.
sentences.l: Onan river up going, Botoqan-Boγ̇orži-at, appointed-place-at, let-us-join" saying, speaking, sent.
sentences.i: let us go up the Onan to Botoqan-Boqorji and join at the place appointed." So he spoke, and sent them off.
sentences.n: odču is od- 'go' with the converb -ču. bolžal γažar-a is 'appointment-place-in', the place agreed on. neiledüje is neile- 'join' with -dü- and the hortative -je (Ming 相合咱). The quotation closes at keġen; ügüležü ilebe is 'speaking, sent', the whole scene as a messenger scene ending in the past tense. The Ming for the last word, ilebe, is 去了.

to join, to come together [相合咱]

sentences.i: When Jamuqa's words had been brought to him, Qan To'oril mounted with two tümens.

sentences.t: Toγ̇oril Qān morilarun Burqan-Qaldun-u ebür Kelüren-ü Burgi ergi žorin aiši keġen
sentences.l: Toγ̇oril Qān when-mounting, Burqan-Qaldun's front, Kelüren's Burgi bank, pointing, "come" saying,
sentences.i: When Qan To'oril rode out, he pointed to the Burgi bank of the Kelüren, in front of Burqan Qaldun, and said, "Come!"
